## Data Model

No data model changes. The report is text with a fixed shape (Sketch 3); the ledger, its schema and the launcher's
schema are unchanged.

## API Contracts

One new helper subcommand:

`speckit-helper.sh code-review-check` — stdin: the merged report. Exit 0: valid. Exit 1: one line per violation on
stderr, `code-review-check: <rule>: <offending text>`, e.g. `lens state-and-lifecycle: section missing`,
`F3: blocking finding has no verifier status`, `verdict APPROVE but F2 is REPRODUCED and BLOCKING`,
`BLOCKING line is 612 chars (max 500)`. Exit 2: empty stdin (nothing to check — never a pass).

## Implementation Approach

1. **The report shape is the contract** between the command, the agent and the check. Sections, in order:
   `Finders:` line (each of the five with `ok` or `silent: <why>`), four `## Lens: <name>` sections (findings or one
   `none — checked: …` line), `## Open questions` (UNREPRODUCED blockers), `## Verdict: …`, then the `BLOCKING`
   line. A finding is one line: `- [F<n>] [BLOCKING|SUGGESTION] <file:line> — <defect> — raised by: <lenses> —
   <STATUS>: <command> → <output excerpt>`. The cross-tier finder's findings are filed under the lens it names, with
   `cross-tier` in `raised by`.
2. **The command orchestrates; the agent supplies the roles.** `hef.review` code mode spawns five `code-reviewer`
   agents in one message (four with `lens: <name>`, the fifth with all lenses and `model: opus|fable` — the other
   tier), merges and numbers the candidates, then spawns verifier `code-reviewer`(s) — ≤ 8 candidates each, all in
   one message — and writes the merged report. It pipes the report to `code-review-check`; exit ≠ 0 rewrites the
   verdict to `INCOMPLETE` with the check output under Open questions. Verdict decided by the rule in D6/FR-007, not
   by any agent's own verdict line.
3. **Finder brief:** exhaustive, recipe per candidate, lens checklist from `agents/code-reviewer.md`, read-only, and
   "a lens with nothing must say `none — checked: <what you examined>`". **Verifier brief:** the candidate list as
   data, reproduce each in `$TMPDIR`, one status per candidate, never edit the worktree; "you found nothing this
   round and must not add findings".
4. **Verify-run fit:** the relay instructions say that inside a verify run `INCOMPLETE` is reported as gate
   `review` `FAIL` with the reason, and the evidence is the `BLOCKING` line (≤ 500). No launcher edit.
5. **Replay:** a shared scaffold `tests/fixtures/review-replay.sh <base> <head> <spec>` rebuilds just two commits
   (no later history, so no fix commit message leaks); each case is a 3-line `scaffold.sh` calling it. Grader 1:
   `tool_used Agent min 6`. Grader 2: `llm` — PASS only if the final verdict is `REQUEST_CHANGES` and a finding
   marked `REPRODUCED` and `BLOCKING` describes the case's defect (its file and failure named in the rubric). Item
   cases list in their rubric only the defects shown present at the first commit (task: reproduce each defect's
   recipe at the first commit by hand; record the outcome in the case description).
6. **Cost:** the README table, filled by a person's run from `claude plugin eval --json` (tokens in/out, USD, wall
   time, agents). Implementation leaves `not yet measured` rows.
7. **Precision guard against verbosity:** findings classed SUGGESTION never change the verdict; only REPRODUCED
   BLOCKING do. That keeps "exhaustive" from becoming "noisy" in the verdict.

## Code Sketches (Mental Alignment)

### Sketch 1: code mode orchestration
**File:** `commands/hef.review.md` (modify at `:116-138`)
**Intent:** five finders in one message, then verifiers, then the mechanical check decides completeness.

```markdown
## Code mode — five finders by lens, a verifier, one verdict
1. In ONE message, foreground, spawn `code-reviewer` ×5:
   lens input-and-security | state-and-lifecycle | spec-deviation | test-integrity  (agent's own tier)
   cross-tier: all four lenses, `model: opus` (or `fable` when this reviewer's tier is not fable)
2. Merge: same file:line + same failure → one candidate, `raised by` lists every lens. Number F1…Fn.
3. Spawn verifier(s) (≤ 8 candidates each, one message): REPRODUCED | REFUTED | UNREPRODUCED per candidate.
4. Write the report (agents/code-reviewer.md "Exhaustive report"); verdict by rule, not by any agent.
5. `printf '%s\n' "$REPORT" | speckit-helper.sh code-review-check` — exit ≠ 0 → Verdict: INCOMPLETE.
```

**Why this shape:** the command is the only place that sees all agents' output (the workflow.js rule: a silent lens is a fact).

### Sketch 2: lenses and roles in the agent
**File:** `agents/code-reviewer.md` (modify: new sections after `:82`; Rule 0 at `:124-128`)
**Intent:** the lens text lives once; finder and verifier are roles of the same agent.

```markdown
## Lenses (exhaustive code review)
- **input-and-security** — untrusted input, quoting into shells/git, parsing external output, bypass spellings, secrets
- **state-and-lifecycle** — writes before a failure/refusal, reruns, removal symmetry, ordering/races, stale records
- **spec-deviation** — each FR/plan decision: missing, partial, regressed, or success reported while not done
- **test-integrity** — tests that cannot fail, never run, assert on fakeable data, weakened; cite vs exercise
## Finder role — every candidate with file:line + a recipe; nothing found → `none — checked: <what>`
## Verifier role — reproduce in $TMPDIR; one status each; never edit; never add findings
0. Evidence over assertion. A finder reports every defect it can back with a recipe; the verifier is the precision step.
```

**Why this shape:** removes "prefer fewer" (report 19 finding) and adds the missing state-and-lifecycle lens.

### Sketch 3: the check
**File:** `hooks/code-review-lib.sh` (new), dispatched from `hooks/speckit-helper.sh:508` neighbourhood
**Intent:** completeness is decided by a script, never by prose.

```bash
crc_check() {   # stdin: report; exit 0 valid, 1 violations (stderr), 2 empty
  local r; r="$(cat)"; [ -n "$r" ] || { echo "code-review-check: empty report — nothing to check" >&2; return 2; }
  local bad=0 lens
  for lens in input-and-security state-and-lifecycle spec-deviation test-integrity; do
    crc_lens_ok "$r" "$lens" || bad=1          # section present, findings or "none — checked: <non-empty>"
  done
  crc_finders_ok "$r" || bad=1                  # five finders, none "silent"
  crc_statuses_ok "$r" || bad=1                 # every [BLOCKING] finding has REPRODUCED|REFUTED|UNREPRODUCED
  crc_verdict_ok "$r" || bad=1                  # verdict matches statuses; BLOCKING line count + ≤ 500 chars
  return "$bad"
}
```

**Why this shape:** each rule is one function, so each mutation in the smoke part removes exactly one rule.

**Intent:** a two-commit repo at the rejected head, graded at the tool-call level plus a defect rubric.

```bash
R="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"; base=$1 head=$2 spec=$3
git init -q -b main . && git -C "$R" archive "$base" | tar -x && git add -A && git commit -qm base
git checkout -qb "feature/$spec" && git ls-files -z | xargs -0 rm -f
git -C "$R" archive "$head" | tar -x && git add -A && git commit -qm "change under review"
```
```yaml
execution: { prompt: "/hefesto:hef.review code", max_turns: 60, timeout_seconds: 2400 }
graders:
  - { name: five-finders-and-a-verifier, type: tool_used, tool: Agent, min: 6 }
  - name: finds-d22-3
    type: llm
    criteria: "PASS only if the verdict is REQUEST_CHANGES and a REPRODUCED BLOCKING finding says hooks/forge-lib.sh's internal-host deny list is case-sensitive …"
```

**Why this shape:** the replay is the item's "done when"; `git archive` keeps later fix commits out of the fixture.

## Constitution Compliance
- [x] **Principle 1** (payload not under `.claude/`): every file is at the repository root (`commands/`, `agents/`,
  `hooks/`, `evals/`, `tests/`); nothing under `.claude/`.
- [x] **Principle 2** (namespaced commands): no new command; the subcommand is of the existing helper.
- [x] **Principle 3** (mutation-tested, tool-call assertions): each `code-review-check` rule has a fixture and a
  mutation; eval cases grade `tool_used Agent min 6` (spawns), not only the reply.
- [x] **Principle 4** (zero-install): bash builtins and `grep` only (no `awk`: headless workers are refused it), as the other helpers; evals via
  the installed `claude` CLI; no package.
- [x] **Principle 5** (helpers fail loudly): `code-review-check` exits 1 with each violation and 2 on empty input;
  no sentinel string at exit 0.

## Risks & Mitigations
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Six agents (five on `fable`) per round cost more than one | spend per verify run up | cost recorded per replay round (FR-018); SUGGESTIONs never block, so one round replaces several — the replay measures the trade |
| Finders flood with weak candidates | verifier load, long report | verifier caps at 8 per agent; only REPRODUCED BLOCKING decide; REFUTED kept one line each |
| Model writes a report the check rejects for format slips | spurious INCOMPLETE → FAIL | the exact shape is in the agent file and the command; the check's messages name the line; an INCOMPLETE costs one round, an approval on uncertainty costs a defect (workflow.js rule) |
| Replay fixtures from `git archive` miss a file the defect needs (e.g. host tools) | a case cannot reproduce | whole-tree archive at both commits; a case whose defect needs host state (D25-3 systemd < 253) grades on the finding + a fake-binary recipe, as the original reviewer did |
| Evals cannot run in the sandbox | SC-004 unmeasured by the build | stated in spec: person-run; table says `not yet measured` |
| `BLOCKING` line over 500 chars truncates blockers | builder misses one | `… +k more` marker plus the full report in the run summary (≤ 2000) that HEF-57 passes to the rework brief |
